Project_Overviews.Title: Evaluating early marine growth and size/condition as an indicator of overall survival in Puget Sound Chinook Salmon
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: Researchers investigated whether the link between juvenile salmon marine performance and marine survival is best indexed by individual growth or size, independently, or by assessing size, growth, and the interactions between them.

Project_Overviews.Title: Evaluating the effects of experimental hatchery management on hatchery Chinook salmon
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: Researchers investigated the effects of experimental hatchery rearing and release strategies on survival and size- and age-at-return of hatchery Chinook salmon as part of an ongoing, multi-year study.

Project_Overviews.Title: Yearling Chinook salmon habitat use in the Skagit River
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: Researchers analyzed six seasons of field observations of stream-type juvenile Chinook salmon habitat use. Understanding the habitat characteristics preferred by juvenile salmon can inform habitat restoration site selection and construction.

Project_Overviews.Title: Investigation of sediment contaminant impacts on the growth and survival of juvenile Puget Sound Chinook salmon
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This study investigated how food restrictions and exposures to toxics in sediments impact juvenile physiology, health, and performance.

Project_Overviews.Title: Modeling population-level impacts from Contaminants of Emerging Concern exposures to endangered salmonids
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: Developing a population model to analyze how exposures to CECs under different scenarios affect population outcomes and stable age distributions in two Puget Sound watersheds.

Project_Overviews.Title: Impacts of spring storms on juvenile salmon health in an urbanized watershed
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project includes field exposures, water quality sampling, and laboratory exposure studies to better understand the risks of stormwater runoff and 6PPD-quinone on juvenile coho salmon.

Project_Overviews.Title: Evaluation of experimental hatchery rearing strategies to benefit Chinook salmon in Puget Sound
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: Researchers investigated the effects of experimental hatchery rearing and release strategies on survival and size- and age-at-return of hatchery Chinook salmon as part of an ongoing, multi-year study.

Project_Overviews.Title: Testing cumulative effects of restoration for multiple salmon populations in the Whidbey Basin using causal analysis
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project will evaluate causal relationships within the Whidbey basin cumulative effects evaluation study hypotheses. This project will evaluate how cumulative restoration is increasing the availability and structure of intertidal habitats for juvenile Chinook. Additionally, this work will evaluate how juvenile Chinook use restored habitats, which salmonid populations in Puget Sound are using these sites, and document the various benefits from the implementation of cumulative nearshore restoration actions over time in the Whidbey basin.

Project_Overviews.Title: Using bioenergetics and landscape connectivity to plan effective tidal delta restoration projects for Chinook salmon under a changing climate
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project is developing an analytical framework using hydraulic, landscape connectivity-abundance, and bioenergetic models to compare the abundance and growth potential of juvenile Chinook salmon across a suite of restoration and climate scenarios.

Project_Overviews.Title: Investigation of sediment contaminant impacts on the growth and survival of juvenile Puget Sound Chinook salmon
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: Researchers are evaluating how Duwamish River sediment impacts the survival of invertebrate prey species for Chinook salmon, and how contaminated prey and reduced food availability impact the physiology and health of juvenile salmon.

Project_Overviews.Title: Nearshore Summit and Synthesis
Project_Overviews.Point of Contact: Tish Conway Cranos, Jason Toft, David Trimbach
Project_Overviews.Affiliation: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife,
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: The goals of this virtual summit were to synthesize nearshore science and restoration actions in Puget Sound and create a roadmap that updates restoration conceptual models and identifies uncertainties to address.

Project_Overviews.Title: Fundamental Environmental Contextual Metrics Dashboard
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project uses data from oceanographic and atmospheric measurement programs to develop six fundamental environmental metrics and compare current status to historical values.  The metrics include estuarine flow, temperature changes from surface heat fluxes, salinity changes from rivers and rain, water column dissolved oxygen, and ocean boundary conditions.

Project_Overviews.Title: Marine Waters Annual 2021 Overview
Project_Overviews.Affiliation: Padilla Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve, University of Washington
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: The Puget Sound Marine Waters Overview report, prepared by the Puget Sound Ecosystem Monitoring Program’s Marine Waters Work Group, provides a comprehensive overview of marine conditions in 2021.

Project_Overviews.Title: Avian Habitat Suitability Models for Puget Sound Estuary Birds
Project_Overviews.Affiliation: Stillaguamish Tribe of Indians, Audobon Washington
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: Puget Sound and the Salish Sea support significant concentrations of shorebirds, waterfowl, and other marine bird species. This project develops science products that support the management needs of estuary birds.

Project_Overviews.Title: Prioritization of Contaminants of Emerging Concern
Project_Overviews.Affiliation: University of Washington, Western Washington University
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project prioritizes contaminants of emerging concern (CECs) for monitoring efforts and management responses. In this project, we aim to use a risk-based approach to identify those CECs which might be most likely to harm fish and other aquatic species. In that way we can more-readily develop solutions to keep them out of the environment.

Project_Overviews.Title: Juvenile Salmonid Monitoring in Large Puget Sound Rivers
Project_Overviews.Point of Contact: Joe Anderson, Pete Lisi, Dawn Pucci
Project_Overviews.Affiliation: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife, Island County
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: Juvenile salmonid monitoring is a key part of understanding freshwater productivity and marine survival of Chinook salmon. For this project, tribal and state smolt trap operators helped identify trends in Chinook salmon abundance and productivity across multiple rivers in Puget Sound.

Project_Overviews.Title: Birds Vital Sign, Abundance of marine birds indicator
Project_Overviews.Affiliation: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: The goal of this project was to support the processing annual mid-winter WDFW PSAMP seabird and waterfowl survey flight data; marine and terrestrial bird indicator updates; winter birds web map; Pigeon Guillemot citizen science data gathering, storage and summary tools.

Project_Overviews.Title: Drinking Water Vital Sign, Index of vulnerability for elevated nitrates in groundwater indicator
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: The goal of this project was to produce a model for an index of vulnerability to nitrates in groundwater and the first Vital Sign Indicator report for the vulnerability index Indicator.

Project_Overviews.Title: Outdoor Activities Vital Sign, Condition of swimming beaches indicator
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: The goal of this project was to support monitoring, data compilation, analyses, and reporting at Puget Sound marine beaches for fecal indicator bacteria, and communication to the public when a risk of disease was identified.

Project_Overviews.Title: Shoreline Armor Vital Sign, HPA based indicator of new and removed armor
Project_Overviews.Affiliation: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: The goal of this project was to support HPA-based data compilation; Vital Sign Indicator reporting for 2019 and 2020; and a Vital Sign decadal summary report and final data product.

Project_Overviews.Title: Cultural Wellbeing, Good Governance, Sense of Place, Sound Stewarship, Local Foods, and Outdoor Activity Vital Signs, subjective human wellbeing indicators
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: The goal of this project was to support a second survey and report in support of the subjective human wellbeing indicators. Reported on Cultural Wellbeing, Good Governance, Sense of Place, Sound Stewardship, Local Foods and Outdoor Activity Vital Signs.

Project_Overviews.Title: Toxics in Fish Vital Sign, Contaminants in juvenile salmon indicator
Project_Overviews.Affiliation: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project assessed compatibility of historical data and assessed time trends. The project included an indicator update for contaminants in juvenile salmon and a draft manuscript and communication product.

Project_Overviews.Title: Developing zooplankton Puget Sound Vital Sign indicators
Project_Overviews.Point of Contact: Julie Kiester, Bethel-Lee Herrmann, Phil Dionne, Correigh Greene, Stu Munsch
Project_Overviews.Affiliation: University of Washington, Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife, National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: A project to develop three Vital Sign Indicators for zooplankton with leadership, information, and data sharing from the Puget Sound Zooplankton Monitoring Program.

Project_Overviews.Title: Puget Sound primary productivity, phytoplankton monitoring and indicators development workshops
Project_Overviews.Point of Contact: Jude Apple, Ashley Bagley, Julia Bos, Cheryl Greengrove, Lucas Hall
Project_Overviews.Affiliation: Padilla Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve, University of Washington, Long Live the Kings, King County
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: A collaborative project to conduct a series of workshops to understand the common measurements to develop a phytoplankton and primary productivity Vital Sign. This will improve the ability to identify spatial and temporal patterns in phytoplankton communities across the region and detect changes in response large-scale and regional climatic and environmental perturbations

Project_Overviews.Title: Enhancing the Human Wellbeing Vital Sign through inclusive engagement
Project_Overviews.Affiliation: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: The highly collaborative project sought to enhance our knowledge of local communities’ human wellbeing in connection to the Vital Signs.  The project used a community-based participatory research (CBPR) approach to inclusively engage residents in Puget Sound.

Project_Overviews.Title: Develop foundation to monitor noise in marine water Vital Sign indicator
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: A project to develop an approach for assessing and reporting on ocean noise levels in Puget Sound as a foundation for the noise in marine water Vital Sign Indicator.

Project_Overviews.Title: Puget Sound Marine Benthic Index and Graphical Causal Model
Project_Overviews.Affiliation: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife, United States Geological Survey
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: A project to develop a Marine Benthic Index Indicator which included modeling species occurrences in relationship to the environment and human disturbance.

Project_Overviews.Title: Compiling and analyzing data for the new Puget Sound salmon Vital Sign indicators
Project_Overviews.Affiliation: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: A project to compile data for the development of Vital Sign Indicators of salmon species abundance. The project also develops a novel spatio-temporal steelhead spawning ground model to improve and expand steelhead abundance estimate

Project_Overviews.Title: Designing a toxics biological monitoring program for the nearshore to accelerate recovery of Puget Sound ecosystem health
Project_Overviews.Point of Contact: James West, Mariko Langness, Louisa Harding, Sandra O'Neill, Mark Scheuerell
Project_Overviews.Affiliation: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife, University of Washington
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: A project to integrate toxics-related biophysical targets with human wellbeing goals by connecting and communicating directly with communities most affected by toxics in the nearshore.

Project_Overviews.Title: Open knowledge networks to support regulatory best available science
Project_Overviews.Point of Contact: Max Lambert, Paul Cereghino, Josh Chamberlin, Stephanie Ehinger
Project_Overviews.Affiliation: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife, National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: A project to develop an iterative conversation between regulators and scientists from multiple agencies around focused topics such as beach nourishment and non-natal habitat use by juvenile salmon outside of their natal watershed.

Project_Overviews.Title: Trophic linkages between zooplankton, herring, and salmon Vital Sign indicators
Project_Overviews.Point of Contact: Correigh Greene, Todd Sandell, Julie Keister
Project_Overviews.Affiliation: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife, University of Washington
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: A project that synthesized data related to Pacific herring, Chinook salmon, other competitors, and zooplankton to understand the trophic linkages in the food web.

Project_Overviews.Title: Developing groundfish and benthic invertebrate Vital Sign indicators for Puget Sound using bottom trawl survey data spanning 36 years
Project_Overviews.Affiliation: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: A project to produce a suite of indices for key species to collectively serve as the ‘Groundfish and Benthic Invertebrates’ Vital Signs indicators using the WDFW Puget Sound Bottom trawl data

Project_Overviews.Title: Puget Sound phytoplankton/primary productivity Vital Sign indicator development - Phase 2: Data Synthesis
Project_Overviews.Affiliation: Padilla Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve, Washington Department of Ecology
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: A project to conduct analyses in support of developing a phytoplankton-based Vital Sign indicator by analyzing the inventory of Puget Sound data established as part of Phase 1. The analysis will identify spatial and temporal patterns and trends in phytoplankton community metrics, reveal data gaps, and explore opportunities for application of emergent data collection methods.

Project_Overviews.Title: Shoreline Armoring trends to inform beaches and marine vegetation Vital Sign indicators in Puget Sound, WA
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be:
A project to leverage recently acquired shoreline armor mapping that documents changes, collect new repeat shoreline armor mapping in under-sampled, represented areas, and then use
the synthesis of data to analyze the trends in armor in the Puget Sound region. It provides a comprehensive, holistic sense of armor trends in Puget Sound, while not having to map every mile of the shore.

Project_Overviews.Title: Monitoring and evaluating adaptive management strategies at two restoration projects in the Skagit Delta
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: A project to extend post restoration effectiveness monitoring of adaptive management strategies designed to improve habitat rather than create new habitat (i.e. via dike breaching or dike setbacks). By continuing monitoring of two sites outside the dike footprint that have recently undergone adaptive management efforts, the objective is to establish a measure of effect at these two sites utilizing a before-after/control-impact (BACI) design.

Project_Overviews.Title: Operationalizing the Salish Sea Estuaries Avian Monitoring Framework
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: A project that takes the first step in operationalizing the Salish Sea Estuaries Monitoring Framework. The project facilitates partnership development, establishes new monitoring sites and train personnel, creates a regional database, and seeks resources (e.g., volunteers, funding) for continued support and on-the-ground assistance.

Project_Overviews.Title: Development of robust estimate of Orca (Orcinus orca) occupancy in Puget Sound
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: A project to develop a robust annual occupancy metric for each of the Southern Resident killer whale and Transient/Bigg’s killer whale ecotypes in central Salish Sea that accurately informs PSP’s new Orca Vital Sign indicators.

Project_Overviews.Title: Human Wellbeing and environmental effects of green infrastructure
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project fills key information gaps in environmental and human well-being benefits of urban green infrastructure by conducting a study of integrated socio-environmental effects of urban trees, tree plantings, and green street installation in rapidly changing South Tacoma. Measures assessed include temperature reduction and psychological well-being associated with tree and canopy characteristics.

Project_Overviews.Title: Sea lion abundance in Puget Sound
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: California sea lion (Zalophus californianus) and the Steller sea lion (Eumetopias jubatus) breed elsewhere, but they typically move into Puget Sound and adjacent waters of the Salish Sea from autumn through spring. This study estimated current abundance and seasonal use patterns of both species, which prey heavily on threatened/endangered stocks of salmon and steelhead trout (Oncorhynchus spp.).

Project_Overviews.Title: Using bioenergetics to plan effective restoration projects for Chinook salmon
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be:
This project developed an analytical framework using landscape connectivity-abundance and bioenergetic models to compare the abundance and growth potential of juvenile Chinook Salmon across a suite
of restoration and climate scenarios for the Stillaguamish estuary. This phase of a larger project provides preliminary results, includin ghydrological modeling for one landscape scenario, landscape connectivity metrics, and bioenergetic model results for one landscape scenario; and a description of ongoing additional studies to fill gaps.

Project_Overviews.Title: Modeling cumulative effects to guide Southern Resident Killer Whale recovery
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This study constructed an updated population viability analysis (PVA) for Southern Resident Killer Whales (SRKWs) to understand the relative importance of anthropogenic threats, and to quantify the amount of mitigationof threats (singly or in combination) it would take to promote SRKW recovery.

Project_Overviews.Title: Prioritization of Contaminants of Emerging Concern
Project_Overviews.Affiliation: Western Washington University, University of Washington
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project advanced the prioritization of contaminants of emerging concern (CECs) for Puget Sound by: improving the spatial extent of samples and contaminants evaluated; evaluating which matrices best represent environmental data; evaluating harm associated with CEC mixtures; and developing an approach to apply this assessment to Endangered Species Act (ESA) listed Southern Resident Killer Whales (SRKW).

Project_Overviews.Title: Qualitative social science through the Skagit story
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This interdisciplinary study updates and expands prior work to investigate conflict in the efforts to recover salmon in the Skagit watershed. This draws from multiple fields across the environmental social sciences and humanities: the environmental history of the American West; ‘first world’ political ecology; social studies of environmental science and conservation; conflict studies; rural sociology; environmental politics; performance studies; humanistic studies of the Anthropocene; inter- andtransdisciplinarity; sustainability; social-ecological systems; science communication; Native American and indigenous studies; settler-colonial studies; and environmental justice.

Project_Overviews.Title: Synthesis of marine survival research findings and Atlantis modeling
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project involved two types of synthesis across the Salish Sea Marine Survival project: a written synthesis of more than 90 individual studies and advancing and applying a Puget Sound version of the Atlantis food web modeling.

Project_Overviews.Title: Path to Adulthood: Comparisons of early marine growth in juveniles versus surviving adults for Chinook and coho
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This study compared stage-specific growth from the juvenile growth regions on scales of Chinook and coho salmon from ocean entry years (OEY) 2014 and 2015.  Juvenile growth patterns were compared to those of the returning adults (i.e., those that survived size-selective mortality through marine life stages) for hatchery or wild stocks from the Nooksack, Skagit, Snohomish, and Nisqually watersheds.

Project_Overviews.Title: Update and maintain smolt-to-adult survival estimates for coded-wire tagged coho and Chinook salmon in coastal Washington and BC
Project_Overviews.Affiliation: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project developed up-to-date estimates of marine survival rates for Washington State coho and Chinook salmon.

Project_Overviews.Title: Examine variability in marine survival of Salish Sea, coastal Washington and BC, and lower Columbia River Chinook salmon associated with biotic and abiotic factors
Project_Overviews.Affiliation: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be:
This project sought to explore how Salish Sea; British Columbia (BC), Washington, and Oregon coast; and Columbia River basin Chinook and coho marine survival
trends have varied over time in association with the presence of juvenile pink salmon, juvenile pink salmon abundance, ecosystem conditions, and the density of conspecifics

Project_Overviews.Title: Herring egg mortality: investigating surf scoter predation on herring eggs at Cherry Point, WA
Project_Overviews.Affiliation: Western Washington University, Washington Department of fish and Wildlife
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This multi-party study: identified the extent and location of Cherry Point herring spawn and spawn duration in relation to bird presence/abundance; analyzed stomach contents of Surf Scoters,;designed and deployed an experiment to investigate the extent of egg predation by Surf Scoters; surveyed and estimated the abundances of birds before, during, and after herring spawning; construct, deploy and monitor an artificial spawning habitat; analyzed the above to understand the effects of scoter predation on herring eggs

Project_Overviews.Title: Pinniped foraging hotspot map: implications for recovering declining salmon stocks
Project_Overviews.Affiliation: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife, University of Washington
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This study employed hierarchical distance sampling methods to 1) estimate the seasonal abundance of harbor seals, 2) identify the areas of high and low densities (i.e., hotspots and coldspots) of harbor seals by season, and 3) identify environmental covariates associated with variation in densities of harbor seals.

Project_Overviews.Title: Determining local sex ratios and sex-specific predation by harbor seals in the Salish Sea of Washington State
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This study expands a prior analysis to a much larger and geographically and temporally diverse sample of seal scats from the Salish Sea of Washington State to address three main questions: 1. Was there spatiotemporal variation in seal sex ratio across the sampling region and time period? 2. Was there sex-specific bias in the prey composition? 3. Were there differences in the intrapopulation feeding diversity between males and females?

Project_Overviews.Title: Spatio-temporal in-water abundance and density estimate of harbor seals during 2013-16 aerial surveys in Puget Sound
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This study used a non-traditional approach to estimate the size of Washington inland waters harbor seal stocks.

Project_Overviews.Title: Measuring the effectiveness of Acoustic Startle Device (ASD) as an acoustic deterrent to reduce predation of wild Chinook, coho, and sockeye salmon by pinnipeds at the Ballard Locks in Seattle, WA
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project tested the effectiveness of the Targetd Acoustic Startle Technology (TAST) in deterring harbor seals from predating on adult salmon at the Hiram M. Chittenden (Ballard) Locks. This was accomplished by collecting behavioral observations and fish counts, and estimating the effect of the TAST on four response variables: 1) Seal presence (counts), 2) Seal distance from the device, 3) Predation events, and 4) Fish passage through the ladder.

Project_Overviews.Title: Deploying the ASD to evaluate its effectiveness in deterring pinniped predation and its effect on steelhead behavior at the Nisqually estuary
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This study deployed and operated a custom-build acoustic deterrent device and monitored the impacts of the device's operation on seal behavior.

Project_Overviews.Title: Evaluate shoreline management in approaches in Clallam and Jefferson counties
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project aimed to evaluate long-term efforts to protect nearshore areas of Clallam and Jefferson counties, especially through the implementation of updated Shoreline Master Programs. Staffing changes and delays in updating the programs led to the cancellation of this project.

Project_Overviews.Title: Whidbey Basin cumulative effects evaluation (study design)
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project provided coordination support for  a multi-party, multi-year project to evaluate the cumulative effects of nearshore habitat restoration in the Whidbey basin. The study rationale, scope, and preliminary analytical framework for the Whidbey basin cumulative effects evaluation was developed through this effort.

Project_Overviews.Title: Change in land cover along salmon streams
Project_Overviews.Affiliation: Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project assessed (1) certainty associated with National Hydrologic Dataset (NHD) accuracy and developed tools and recommendations for updating it using a mix of remote sensing, modeling and field work and (2) the status of riparian critical areas, their recent rates of change, and sources of error that might reduce confidence in these estimates

Project_Overviews.Title: Effectiveness of shellfish protection districts and other shellfish bed restoration efforts
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This study 1) captured regional perceptions of the effectiveness of recovery and long-term protection efforts intended to restore Puget Sound shellfish beds to harvestable condition and 2) developed recommendations to enhance regional shellfish recovery action effectiveness based on interview data.

Project_Overviews.Title: Coordinate 2019-2021 Salish Sea marine survival efforts
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: Puget Sound Scientific Research funds were first appropriated to the Puget Sound Partnership in 2019-2021. To get the funding program underway, the Partnership collaborated closely with the Salish Sea Marine Survival Project's coordinating and technical committees to understand research needs and coordinate the selection of projects to receive funding.

Project_Overviews.Title: Distribution of current and future risk of anthropogenic and climate change threats to marine vegetation In Puget Sound
Project_Overviews.Affiliation: University of Washington Puget Sound Institute
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be:
This project will conduct a cumulative, spatially explicit risk analysis of eelgrass and kelp habitats around Puget Sound to support conservation and restoration decisions. It builds on past work identifying threats to
eelgrass and kelp and leverages existing spatial datasets of species distributions and current and future threats.

Project_Overviews.Title: Human use of water in Puget Sound: Role of water demand management in building community and ecosystem resilience in a changing climate
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project uses future scenario analysis to develop spatially explicit estimates of the changes in residential water use possible via demand management and managed growth and the sensitivity of those estimates to changes in population, two climate scenarios, and varying adoption of demand management strategies within Puget Sound. An assessment of the potential for water reclamation is conducted in parallel.

Project_Overviews.Title: Optimizing green stormwater infrastructure (GSI) placement: A dynamic landscape indexing approach
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project will merge the results from two prior studies to provide a more comprehensive framework for green stormwater infrastructure (GSI) and tree placement; layer data from the latest environmental health disparities information to create priority zones; and build predicted temperatures, rainfall totals, and intensities due to climate change into the framework.

Project_Overviews.Title: Synthesis of restoration effectiveness in estuary and nearshore habitats in Puget Sound
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project will conduct a systematic evidence-based literature review and meta-analysis of habitat monitoring, salmon response, and restoration effectiveness data in Puget Sound tidal delta and nearshore habitats.

Project_Overviews.Title: Using remote sensing to quantify the hydrogeomorphic response of historically disconnected habitats in the Dungeness River floodplain following restoration of hydrologic connectivity
Project_Overviews.Affiliation: North Olypmic Peninsula Lead Entity for Salmon
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project aims to document the hydrogeomorphic response of historically disconnected habitats in the Dungeness River floodplain following restoration of hydrologic connectivity to the mainstem river.

Project_Overviews.Title: Advancing future scenarios
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project augments ongoing Puget Sound Future Scenarios work to extend the ability of the model to illuminate important issues and questions of great importance to the Puget Sound recovery community, including improving representation and analysis of shoreline and nearshore features (particularly estuaries) and processes; identifying and accurately representing important habitat for salmon; developing and implementing capacity to better assess socio-economic factors and tradeoffs and to assess changes in housing affordability, and investigating the utility and feasibility of a desktop interface for Future Scenario tools

Project_Overviews.Title: Estimating potential changes in stream drying under future drought conditions for streams in the Puget Sound region
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project will quantify how potential changes in the frequency and severity of drought will change where and when streams have surface water or go dry in the Puget Sound region. This work will identify location and extent of stream reaches that are likely to go dry under future drought conditions and provide information that can inform land use management decisions, how salmon survival may be impacted by future conditions, and track changes in stream habitat viability and impact on streamflow processes.

Project_Overviews.Title: Puget Sound Acidification and Impacts (PSAI): An applied data product for estimating acidification and its impacts in the Puget Sound and surrounding areas
Project_Overviews.Affiliation: University of Washington Cooperative Institute for Climate, Ocean, and Ecosystem Studies
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project will create a tool that will enable estimation of ocean acidification parameters within Puget Sound called Puget Sound Acidification and Impacts (PSAI). The project will work with diverse end users of the tool to co-design and refine the tool for better accessibility to and easier interpretation of acidification data so it may be used to improve management and research capabilities.

Project_Overviews.Title: Healing Women, Healing Mother Earth: A Participatory Mixed Methods Study on Refining Puget Sound Resilience with Indigenous Knowledge Systems
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project will conduct a participatory mixed methods study to refine our understanding of ecosystem resilience with Indigenous Knowledge Systems (IKS) encompassing Indigenous women’s ecosystem management efforts. The project will examine how IKS can inform ecosystem management efforts to link Indigenous stewardship with environment, culture, and well-being  and capture the success stories of Indigenous women’s stewardship efforts to mitigate climate impacts, and display results as a StoryMap.

Project_Overviews.Title: Machine Learning methods to inform toxicity of contaminants of emerging concern
Project_Overviews.Affiliation: University of Washington Puget Sound Institute
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project will evaluate and apply machine learning, and artificial intelligence tools to increase our understanding of the potential biological impacts of Contaminants of Emerging Concern (CEC) on salmonids. Results will be used to address regional gaps in knowledge that currently inhibit the ability ot evaluate CECs in Puget Sound.

Project_Overviews.Title: Quantifying spatio-temporal oceanographic controls on culturally-important fisheries in northern Whidbey Basin
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project will expand water property monitoring in northern Whidbey Basin, determine spatial and temporal trends across estuarine gradients, and assess current and future species habitat vulnerability to variability. The project will provide novel intertidal data and pair it with offshore profiles and buoy data to inform resource managers of the range of physical conditions that species experience, and determine the extent to which tribally-important species are exposed to stressful or lethal conditions.

Project_Overviews.Title: Salmon governance for multispecies planning
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project will use process tracing to analyze data from existing documentation and expert interviews to evaluate correlational and causal inferences between historical salmon policy processes and the outcomes. It will describe the current salmon governance landscape in the transboundary Salish Sea region through a comparative analysis, while elevating multispecies justice thinking within current salmon governance efforts

Project_Overviews.Title: Evaluating experimental hatchery rearing strategies to increase Puget Sound Chinook's resilience to climate change and future ecosystem conditions
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project will synthesize hatchery return data from experimental fish releases conducted by seven hatcheries in 2018-2021 to provide guidance toward optimizing hatchery management strategies and improving marine survival of hatchery fish.

Project_Overviews.Title: Linking spatial distribution and residency of tagged juvenile salmon to adult recruitment and identifying mortality hotspots
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project will expand PIT tagging efforts in the Green River to include mobile tracking, continued juvenile tagging, and the installation of an adult return detection array. Results will be used to link juvenile rearing patterns to adult returns, identify potential mortality hotspots, and identify locations to prioritize for habitat restoration.

Project_Overviews.Title: Addressing water quality impacts on salmonids in runoff-impaired watersheds
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: Building upon previous work on coho salmon, this project will evaluate the impacts of real-time exposures to ambient stream water and roadway runoff in Chinook salmon and steelhead. It will also assess a runoff treatment best management practice to reduce toxic chemical exposure for juvenile salmon.

Project_Overviews.Title: Salmon Stories: Honoring the ancestors, protecting the future
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project will develop a comprehensive awareness campaign highlighting the deep relationship between Native peoples and salmon, tracing this connection from ancestral stewardship to modern conservation efforts. This project will enhance public understanding, strengthen collaborations between tribal and non-tribal entities, and support more inclusive decision-making processes.

Project_Overviews.Title: Cognitive mapping for the co-production of ecosystem-based solutions to salmon recovery and killer whale conservation in Puget Sound
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This study will inform strategies for balancing fisheries sustainability with orca conservation by identifying shared values and areas of contention using social science methods and socio-ecological models.

Project_Overviews.Title: Juvenile salmonid habitat use of bull kelp in Puget Sound: Application to recovery and protection goals
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project will analyze juvenile Chinook salmon abundance and behavior in bull kelp forests at 16 locations in Puget Sound using snorkel surveys and eDNA. Results will be used to develop a connectivity framework, address habitat fragmentation, target areas for conservation and restoration, and identify priorities for future work.

Project_Overviews.Title: Using an individual based model to examine shared benefits of tidal delta and nearshore restoration in the Whidbey Basin
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project will develop an individual based model (IBM) to evaluate benefits of habitat restoration on juvenile Chinook salmon growth and survival in the entire Whidbey Basin. The IBM will evaluate the benefits of changes in connectivity and habitat capacity for individual salmon and cohort survival to better understand intertidal habitat restoration benefits for salmon and prioritize future restoration efforts.

Project_Overviews.Title: Puget Sound Phytoplankton Vital Sign Indicator- Phase 3: Defining metrics and the indicator reporting plan
Project_Overviews.Affiliation: Padilla Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve, Washington Department of Ecology
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project will develop Phase 3 of the Phytoplankton Vital Sign Indicator to ultimately inform a Vital Sign Indicator Report.

Project_Overviews.Title: Drift cell functional condition status reporting and trend development
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project will develop the Drift Cell Functional Condition based on Washington Department of Ecology's ACRE program utilizing data from 360-degree on-the-water photos, oblique shoreline photos, and a shoreline condition survey that documents modifications to the nearshore.

Project_Overviews.Title: Advancing the development of an estuarine bird Puget Sound Vital Sign Indicator
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project will collaborate with the Marine Birds Work Group and connect with the Migratory Shorebird Project to inform on an Esutarine Bird Vital Sign Indicator scoping report.

Project_Overviews.Title: Developing integrated health metrics to inform management of Puget Sound's killer whales
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project will update a web-accessible killer-whale health database and include new datasets realted to killer-whale health to inform on orca management and recovery efforts.

Project_Overviews.Title: Synthesizing and sharing knowledge of Puget Sound Dungeness crab populations with fisheries co-managers
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project aims to increase access to Puget Sound Dungeness crab monitoring information while maintaining data soverignty, enhancing understanding by resource managers and resources users of the dynamics of local Dungeness crab populations, and provide future directions for collaborative research efforts prioritized.

Project_Overviews.Title: Beach Nourishment Effectiveness for Restoration in Puget Sound
Project_Overviews.Affiliation: Natural Systems Design + Coastal Geologic Services
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project aims to support restoration practitioners and coastal managers by improving high-level and project-specific evaluation of restoration proposals with beach nourishment and will allow for more successful work in the future. Deliverables of this work includes a scientific report and a best practices document.

Project_Overviews.Title: Evaluating the impact of scientific uncertainty and conflict on research and decision-making for orca recovery
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: This project will evaluate the impact of scientific uncertainty and conflict on research and decision-making for Southern Resident orca recovery. Objectives include identifying opportunities for reducing uncertainties, informing research priorities, and evaluating coordination and conflict transformation for decision-making when uncertainty is irreducible.

Project_Overviews.Title: Examining LGBTQ+ Access to Green Space in the Puget Sound Region: Challenges and Pathways to Inclusion
Project_Overviews.Description (1-2 sentence overview to be: The research focuses on promoting inclusivity in parks and green spaces by identifying and addressing barriers to access for individuals with marginalized identities.
